overview: August 10 was headlined by Leon Hwang's 13-patch series introducing tracing_multi link support, which lets a single BPF program attach to multiple kernel functions in one link—similar to the existing fentry.multi/fexit.multi mechanism. Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi extended resolve_btfids to emit arena attributes from kfunc parameter suffixes, tightening the tooling side of arena-aware kfuncs. Bug fixes from chenyuan addressed range_tree consistency in the BPF arena allocator and several bpftool batch-file handling regressions, while Jiayuan Chen's series closes a safety gap that allowed hardware-offloaded XDP programs to be attached on-host via tcx or netkit.

patches.title: bpf: Add tracing_multi link support for bpf progs
patches.author: Leon Hwang
patches.summary: Introduces a new BPF_LINK_TYPE_TRACING_MULTI link type that allows a single BPF tracing program to be attached to multiple kernel functions simultaneously, analogous to how fentry.multi and fexit.multi work for trampolines. The implementation extends the existing bpf_trampoline infrastructure with a new tracing_multi path and adds fdinfo and link-info reporting. This removes the need to open and pin separate links per function when tracing many call sites at once. The 13-patch series covers the core kernel changes, libbpf API additions, and a comprehensive selftest suite including rollback, cookie, and tailcall interaction tests.

patches.title: libbpf: Add tracing_multi link support for bpf progs
patches.author: Leon Hwang
patches.summary: Adds the libbpf userspace API for the tracing_multi link type, providing bpf_program__attach_tracing_multi() and related helpers so that user programs can attach a single BPF prog to multiple kernel symbols in one syscall roundtrip. The API mirrors the existing fentry.multi/fexit.multi pattern and integrates with libbpf's existing link lifecycle management. This is the userspace counterpart to the kernel-side tracing_multi link patch and is needed for tools like bpftrace to consume the new feature.

patches.title: resolve_btfids: Emit arena attributes from kfunc parameter suffixes
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: Teaches the resolve_btfids build tool to recognise the __arena and __arena__nullable suffixes on kfunc parameters and emit the corresponding KF_ARENA_RD/KF_ARENA_WR BTF attributes into the kernel's compiled BTF. Without this, the verifier cannot correctly type-check arena pointer arguments to kfuncs at load time. The companion selftest patch verifies that the emitted attributes round-trip correctly through the BTF subsystem. This is a prerequisite tooling piece for the broader arena-argument-in-kfuncs feature being developed by Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi.

patches.title: bpf, tcx, netkit: reject offloaded programs
patches.author: Jiayuan Chen
patches.summary: Fixes a gap where a BPF program compiled for hardware offload (e.g. for a SmartNIC) could be attached on the host via tcx or netkit, where it would run in the kernel without the expected hardware context. The fix adds an offload check early in dev_xdp_install() and propagates the rejection through the tcx and netkit attach paths. The third patch adds a selftest that confirms dev_xdp_install() correctly rejects device-bound programs. This prevents subtle correctness and security issues that could arise from running offloaded programs in the wrong execution environment.

patches.title: bpf, arena: fix range_tree_clear inconsistency on kmalloc_nolock failure
patches.author: chenyuan
patches.summary: Fixes a range_tree state inconsistency in the BPF arena allocator that could occur when kmalloc_nolock() fails inside range_tree_clear() or range_tree_set(). On allocation failure the previous implementation left the range-tree in a partially modified state, potentially corrupting future allocations or frees. The three-patch series also checks the return value of range_tree_set() in arena_free_pages() and arena_free_worker(), ensuring failure is surfaced rather than silently ignored. This is the second version, incorporating review feedback on the original submission.

patches.title: bpftool: fix double close in map dump
patches.author: chenyuan
patches.summary: Corrects a double-close bug in bpftool's map dump path where a file descriptor was closed twice on certain error paths, risking a use-after-free if the fd was reallocated between the two closes. The series (v4 of the submission) also fixes a spurious batch-file read error and a bypass of the batch line-length check when lines contain comments. These are tooling correctness fixes that improve the reliability of bpftool batch mode and map dump operations.

patches.title: selftests/bpf: Add kptr-xchg benchmark
patches.author: Chenguang Zhao
patches.summary: Adds a microbenchmark for the bpf_kptr_xchg() helper to the BPF selftests benchmark suite. The benchmark measures the throughput of atomic pointer exchange operations on BPF map values, providing a baseline for future optimisation work on kernel pointer management in BPF programs. Having a dedicated benchmark makes it straightforward to detect regressions or measure the impact of changes to the kptr locking or reference-counting paths.
